pools.name: The Beast Lands
omens: The grass is flattened in a wide ring, and in its center something has been eating. It lifts its head.
Every bird in the valley falls silent at once. The herd that was grazing is not a herd.
Antlers rise from the bracken, too many of them, and the thing beneath them is smiling.
A carcass hangs in the fork of a tree, fresh, at a height no wolf could reach.
The tracks circle the camp twice and stop. Something breathes behind you, hot and patient.
The wind carries the smell of wet fur and old blood. The hunt has turned around.

pools.name: The Hollow Wood
omens: The trees lean in to listen. Somewhere in the bark, a mouth opens.
A path appears that was not there before, lined with pale mushrooms that turn to watch you pass.
The leaves fall upward. Between the trunks, shapes that were standing very still begin to move.
Sap runs red from a split in the oak, and the oak is screaming.
Seed husks crunch underfoot like knuckles. The undergrowth rustles in every direction at once.
A child's voice calls your names from the dark between the roots. No child lives here.

pools.name: The Drowned Marches
omens: The water is waist-deep and warm as a body. Something brushes your legs and keeps going.
Lanterns bob on the black water, held by no hands. They drift closer.
The reeds part. A face looks up from beneath the surface, and its eyes are open.
Bells toll from a chapel that sank a hundred years ago. The tide is coming in.
Mud sucks at your boots and lets go reluctantly, like something tasting.
Bloated shapes rise from the bog in a slow ring, still wearing what they drowned in.

pools.name: The Barrows
omens: The barrow door is open, and it was sealed from the inside.
Grave-goods glitter in the torchlight. The bones they were buried with sit up.
Dust falls from the ceiling in a steady hiss, as though the earth above is breathing out.
Your torch burns blue. The names carved on the lintel have been scratched out, then carved again, fresher.
Somewhere below, a slow scrape: armor dragging over stone, coming up the stair.
The dead here were buried face down, so they would dig the wrong way. Someone turned them over.

pools.name: The Deep Cold
omens: Your breath freezes into shapes you did not make. The ice beneath you is lit from below.
A frozen army stands in the pass, mid-stride. The nearest one has turned its head since you arrived.
The snow falls without sound, and the footprints ahead of you are your own, walking back.
The cold has teeth tonight. Out on the white, something howls with a human throat.
Blue fire crawls along the glacier's crack. Whatever sleeps inside it is waking hungry.
Frost spreads across your shields in the shape of a hand.

pools.name: The Pit
omens: The heat rises in waves, and in the waves are faces, mouthing your names.
Chains rattle in the dark below, all at once, as if something has stood up.
The walls weep a black oil that smells of tallow and old prayers. The ledge narrows.
Screams echo up the shaft, too regular to be pain. They are counting.
A ring of brass hooks hangs over the drop, each one wet. The pit is feeding.
Embers drift upward against the wind. Below, eyes open in the coals.

pools.name: The Forge Ruins
omens: The great bellows heave on their own. The furnace has been lit for you.
Hammers ring on anvils in an empty hall, keeping time to a heartbeat.
Cold iron limbs lie heaped by the slag pit. Some of them still twitch.
Molten metal runs down the gutters in letters, spelling a word nobody wants to read.
A smith's apron hangs by the door, stiff with blood, still warm.
Gears grind behind the walls. Every door slams shut, one after another, toward you.

pools.name: The Faceless City
omens: The streets are full of people, and none of them has a face. They all turn toward you.
Masks hang from every lintel, and every mask is weeping. The square ahead is too quiet.
A bell rings for a festival. The dancers move without music, and their steps leave stains.
Every window shows the same room, and in every room the same figure rises from its chair.
Your own names are painted on the walls, already crossed out.
A crowd parts in perfect silence. At its heart, something wears the mayor's chain.

pools.name: The Apostate Court
omens: The throne room is lit for a feast. Every guest is dead, and every guest is listening.
A herald announces you by titles you have never held, and the court laughs behind its fans.
Banners of Houses that no longer exist hang from the rafters. Yours is among them.
Wine runs from the fountain thick and dark. The courtiers bow, and keep bowing, until their necks break.
A crown lies on the steps, waiting. Whoever wears it here does not take it off.
The judges in their black hoods have already reached a verdict.

pools.name: The Shrine of Six
omens: Six candles burn on the altar. One for each god, and one that should not be lit.
Hymns rise from the empty pews, in a language that hurts the teeth.
Pilgrims kneel in rows, their foreheads worn to the bone against the stone. They rise as one.
The holy water boils without fire. The saint in the window has turned her back.
Incense thick as wool fills the nave, and something in it is breathing.
The relic in the reliquary blinks.

pools.name: The Dragon Reaches
omens: The mountainside is glassed black, and the glass is still warm.
Bones the size of ship's keels line the pass. Some of them are new.
A shadow passes over the sun, then over you, then circles back.
Gold coins cover the slope like scree, and every one is stamped with a dead king's face. Something stirs under the hoard.
Sulfur stings your eyes. The ground trembles with a slow, enormous breath.
Scales litter the path, shed and sharp as knives. Whatever wore them has grown.

pools.name: The Outer Dark
omens: The stars go out, one by one, until only the eyes are left.
Up and down lose their meaning. A voice speaks from the inside of your skull, gently, like a mother.
Geometry fails. The thing ahead has too many angles, and all of them are looking at you.
You hear your own heartbeat outside your body, and something else is listening to it.
The light from your lanterns bends away from what waits, afraid.
Here at the edge of all things, the Rift is not a door. It is a mouth.
